Team —

Quick status update and proposed split of work:
- Marissa: take lead on the MSA tracked changes (defend vs reimburse variants). I added margin comments in the attached draft.
- Jordan: draft the evidence-preservation checklist and suggested 30-day/60-day SLA language; include examples of logs/forensic exports we can provide.
- Ben: maintain customer comms and consolidate commercial concessions (caps/insurance offsets).

Key legal positions we should preserve in the first draft:
1) Redwood will generally defend when the claim alleges infringement of third-party IP by our underlying models or platform where the claim arises from our modifications/hosting.
2) For claims tied solely to customer-provided prompts/data or customer fine-tuning (including embeddings/data used to create models), default to customer responsibility — but propose a narrow "assistance" cooperation clause.
3) AI-generated output: propose mutual indemnity carveout for purely user-generated prompts; Redwood offers remediation support and limited reimbursement if root cause traces to pre-packaged model training artifacts.
4) Explicit OSS carveout: follow Apache/MIT/BSD exceptions; customer must show provenance.

I attached the draft redline and the checklist template. I've flagged areas where Finance may need to weigh in on cap tradeoffs.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & IP
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Added a couple of commercial options in the redline:
- Option A (Customer-defend for content claims): Redwood offers a limited fee credit tied to the order form if customer agrees to lead defense for content claims resulting from customer prompts.
- Option B (Joint-defense with mediation): Redwood will step in to lead defense for third-party IP claims; if both parties prefer joint defense, include mediation step before cost-splitting kicks in.

Marissa left comments in the MSA redline around insurance offsets and whether we accept subrogation in limited cases. Also added a short blurb to the evidence checklist describing acceptable formats for forensic exports (e.g., JSON logs, raw request captures, model input/response snapshots).

I'll let Jordan finalize the checklist items. Once we have the consolidated doc, Ben can share with Paul, and we can plan a 30-min sync with Orchid's GC to walk the options.
